findings.title: Sign error in the convective boundary condition of the shared thermal definition
findings.detail: docs/thermal_model.md §4 (line 69) states the baseplate-bottom condition as `-k ∂T/∂z = h (T − T_c)` 'with outward normal −z'. With z = 0 at the baseplate bottom and z pointing up (doc §1), the outward heat flux there is q·(−ẑ) = +k ∂T/∂z, so the correct condition is `k ∂T/∂z = h (T − T_c)`, equivalently `-k ∂T/∂n = h (T − T_c)`. As written, a 1D case with heat entering at the top (∂T/∂z > 0) gives T < T_c at the bottom, which is not physical. The formula contradicts the prose on the same line ('the heat flux leaving is h (T − T_c)') and the §3 die-top condition, which uses ∂/∂n correctly. Both solvers (n3, n5) are told to implement 'this document independently', so this defect sits in the shared reference. It is not a blocker: the prose and the required energy-balance self-check would expose a literal implementation at once.
findings.evidence: docs/thermal_model.md:69 vs :63; derivation: heat flux q = −k∇T, outward normal n = −ẑ ⇒ q·n = k ∂T/∂z.
findings.suggested_check: Replace with `-k ∂T/∂n = h (T − T_c)` (n outward, = −z), i.e. `k ∂T/∂z = h (T − T_c)` at z = 0.

findings.title: Al2O3 k(T) citation misquotes Incropera Table A.2, and the 'independent tabulated ratio' test depends on the misquote
findings.detail: stack.py cites Incropera Table A.2 polycrystalline Al2O3 as 36, 26, 15.8 W/(m K) at 300/400/600 K and derives interval exponents −1.13/−1.23. The table value at 400 K is 26.4, which gives −1.08 and −1.27. The fitted exponent −1.15 is still correct for 300–480 K (log-interpolated endpoint fit: −1.151). However, tests/unit/geometry/test_stack.py:83 checks k(400)/k against 26.0/36 with rel=0.015. The model is 2.05 % off the real 26.4/36, so that 'independent' check would fail with the correct table value. It passes only because of the misquote.
findings.evidence: Computed (4/3)^-1.15 = 0.7183; |0.7183/(26/36) − 1| = 0.54 %; |0.7183/(26.4/36) − 1| = 2.05 %. Table row 36.0 / 26.4 / 15.8 confirmed in Scribd copies of Incropera App. A, Table A.2.
findings.suggested_check: Quote 26.4 and the correct exponents, and set the test's reference to 26.4/36 with an honestly stated fit tolerance (≈2.5 %).

findings.title: SAC305 k(T) docstring misstates the slope of the coded law
findings.detail: The stack.py docstring says 'Medium-low confidence in the slope (−7 % between 300 and 480 K)'. The coded law f = (T/300)/(1 + 4.2e-3 (T − 300)) gives f(480)/f(300) = 0.911, i.e. −8.9 %.
findings.evidence: K_LAWS['SAC305'](480)/K_LAWS['SAC305'](300) = 0.91116; the default solder layer goes 58.0 → 52.85 W/(m K).

findings.title: Layer.k_at silently accepts NaN
findings.detail: The range guard `np.any(T < K_T_MIN) or np.any(T > K_T_MAX)` is False for NaN. A diverged Picard iterate fed to k_at therefore returns NaN rather than the documented ValueError.
findings.suggested_check: Reject non-finite T explicitly (e.g. `if not np.all(np.isfinite(T))`).

findings.title: All Layout fingerprints change; stored E002 fingerprints are no longer reproducible
findings.detail: Layout.fingerprint now also hashes stack.die_attach and stack.die, so every existing fingerprint changes. Example: generate_layouts(1, seed=7, family='side_by_side', dies_per_switch=2) goes from 5bcd22a3… (pre-change code, rebuilt in scratch) to 65138a70…. experiments/results/E002/*/e002_rows.json stores fingerprints that current code can no longer regenerate. No test or tool recomputes them today. layout.py and test_layout.py are modified, though neither appears in the deliverables list.
findings.evidence: Pre-change fingerprint computed from a reverse-patched scratch copy of src.
findings.suggested_check: Record in the change log or ADR that fingerprints changed at this commit.

findings.title: Stack die-layer thicknesses are decoupled from the per-die geometry
findings.detail: By design, Die.thickness and Die.attach_thickness rule the geometry. Changing stack.die_attach.thickness (or k) has no effect on EM outputs or on the die z-range, and nothing warns when the two disagree. The doc states this is allowed, but a thermal solver could read the wrong one.
findings.evidence: Mutation check: setting stack.die_attach.thickness = 1 mm, k = 1 left the EM snapshot identical. A +1 µm Die.thickness change was caught (shorts z_top).
findings.suggested_check: Consider a warning or check in the thermal solver when stack and per-die thicknesses differ.

independent_checks_performed: Ran the definition-of-done commands: the pyamg/skfem/sympy import works (5.4.1 / 12.0.2 / 1.14.0); check_licenses blocks nothing (only moduleforge flagged for review); ruff clean; the required pytest selection gives 357 passed, 31 deselected.
uv lock --check --offline: lock consistent with pyproject.

Reverse-applied the packet diff to a scratch copy of src and recomputed the EM snapshot for all 6 cases with pre-change code: exact JSON equality with em_before_thermal_stack.json (the baseline is genuinely pre-change).
Mutation-tested the EM regression compare: Die.thickness +1 µm is caught; a change to the stack die_attach layer alone is (by design) not.

Evaluated k_at for every layer of the DBC and AMB stacks at 273.15/300/400/480/523.15 K; checked the boundary values and an out-of-range array raise ValueError, an unknown material raises KeyError, and NaN passes through.

Re-derived the Cu law against Incropera Table A.1 (393 at 400 K exact; 377 vs 379 at 600 K) and the Al2O3 law against Table A.2 (26.4 at 400 K; fitted exponent −1.151 over 300–480 K); found the test tolerance would fail with the true 26.4.
Computed the SAC305 law ratio 480/300 = 0.911 (docstring says −7 %), and the Wiedemann–Franz check k(300) = 56.3 W/(m K).
Checked the doc §2 containment rules on 72 generated layouts (3 families × {2, 4, 6} dies × 8): no violations. All generated dies use 180 µm / 50 µm.
Hand-derived the sign of the convective and flux boundary conditions in doc §3–4 from q = −k∇T: the die-top flux BC is correct, the baseplate-bottom formula is sign-flipped.
Compared layout fingerprints before and after the change and searched the repo for stored or recomputed fingerprints (E002 rows store them; nothing recomputes them).
Web-verified the Muzychka/Culham/Yovanovich J. Electron. Packag. 125(2):178–185 (2003) citation and the Incropera Table A.2 Al2O3 row.

Ran the non-slow suite over all of tests/ with -x: 146 passed, then 1 failed in tests/mfos/test_sandbox.py::test_with_the_sandbox_disabled_nothing_changes. It asserts UV_OFFLINE is unset, but the review sandbox sets UV_OFFLINE=1; the test covers mfos orchestration code this change does not touch.
caveats: Doc §4 must be read through its prose ('heat flux leaving is h(T − T_c)'), not its formula, until the sign is fixed; downstream solvers n3/n5 should not implement the formula literally.
The Al2O3 law is a 300–480 K fit that is up to about 2 % below Incropera at 400 K (conservative: hotter Tj); the 'independent tabulated' unit test does not actually check against the table value.

The SAC305 and Si3N4 k(T) laws are physically motivated shapes with medium-low and medium confidence, not fits to primary data; the 4H-SiC (T/300)^-1.49 TCAD attribution was not independently verified.
Layout fingerprints differ from those stored in E002 results; any provenance check that regenerates layouts and compares fingerprints across this commit will mismatch.

The full non-slow run over all of tests/ stopped at its first failure after 146 passes: an environment-dependent mfos sandbox test (UV_OFFLINE set by the review sandbox), unrelated to this change. The rest of the wider suite was not exercised here; only the DoD-specified test selection was verified to pass in full.
